examples.en: My friend's name is Kim Minsu.
There is a person called Manager Kim at the company.
Mr. Kim, the owner, is at the restaurant now.
I'll send an email to Professor Kim first.

explain: 성 '김' 뒤에 '선생님, 부장님, 교수님' 같은 직함을 붙여 부르는 경우가 많아요. 성만 부르고 '씨'를 붙이면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어서, 보통 '김민수 씨'처럼 이름까지 말해요. 먹는 김(seaweed)이나 수증기 '김'과 소리가 같아요.

phrases.example: 그런 사람을 찾는 건 서울에서 김 서방 찾기예요.
phrases.en: Finding a person like that is like finding a needle in a haystack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단서가 거의 없어서 어떤 사람이나 물건을 찾기가 매우 어려울 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something or someone is nearly impossible to find because there are hardly any clues.

explain_en: People often call someone by this surname plus a title such as 선생님, 부장님 or 교수님. Using only the surname with '씨' can sound rude, so people usually say the full name, as in '김민수 씨'. It sounds the same as 김 (seaweed) and 김 (steam).
